hook.text: Weather models are among the most demanding users of supercomputers—consuming billions of calculations per forecast.

buildup.text: Each upgrade in computing power allows finer grid spacing—resolving smaller weather features more accurately.

discovery.text: Today's global models run at about 9 km resolution—compared to 300 km in the 1970s, a massive improvement.

twist.text: Despite huge computing gains, forecast models still can't resolve individual thunderstorms—they must be approximated.

climax.text: ECMWF's supercomputer performs over 300 petaflops—yet the atmosphere still has detail that exceeds its resolution.

punchline.text: Faster computers, better forecasts—but the atmosphere stays one step ahead.

quiz.question: Why can't current global models resolve individual thunderstorms?
options: Grid spacing is still too coarse to capture them
